subject: Government
examFormat: The aim of the UTME syllabus in Government is to prepare candidates for the Board’s examination and to test their knowledge of Government with a view to determining their suitability for placement in institutions of higher learning in Nigeria. The general objectives are to appreciate the meaning of Government, analyse the framework and institutions of government, appreciate the principles of democratic governance and their application in Nigeria, explain citizenship and its duties, evaluate Nigeria’s political development and problems of governance, understand the determinants of foreign policy, and assess Nigeria’s role in the international community. The syllabus is in four parts: Elements of Government, Political Development in Nigeria, Foreign Policy and Nigeria’s Relationship with the International Community, and International Organizations. It states no exam format.
recommendedTexts: Essentials of Government for West Africa — F. Adigwe (Ibadan: University Press Plc, 1985)
Elements of Politics — R. Anifowose and F. C. Enemuo (eds) (Lagos: Malthouse Press Limited, 1999)
The Substance of Politics — A. Appadorai (London: Oxford University Press, 1978)
Modern Politics and Government — A. R. Ball (London: Macmillan, 1983)
Government for the Certificate Year — R. Ofoegbu (London: George Allen and Unwin, 1977)
New Topics on Ordinary Level Government — J. B. Olawale (Ilesha: Jola Publishing, 1987)
Government for Senior Secondary Schools, Books 1, 2 and 3 — O. Oyediran, H. Nwosu, B. Takaya, R. Anifowoshe, B. Femi, O. Godwill and A. Adigun (Ibadan: Longman, 1990)
Round-Up Government for Senior Secondary School Certificate Examination: A Complete Guide — I. Oyeneye, M. Onyenwenu and B. E. Olusunde (Ibadan: Longman, 2000)
Countdown to Senior Secondary Certificate Examination: Government — S. Oyovbaire, A. E. C. Ogunna, E. C. Amucheazi, H. O. Coker and O. Oshuntuyi (Ibadan: Evans, 2001)

topics.name: Basic Concepts in Government
objectives: identify the fundamental concepts in governance
analyse various political processes

subtopics.name: Political Processes: Political Socialization, Political Participation, Political Culture

topics.name: Forms of Government
objectives: distinguish between different forms of government
topics.content: Monarchy, Aristocracy, Oligarchy, Autocracy, Republicanism and Democracy: definitions, features, merits and demerits.

topics.name: Arms of Government
objectives: identify the duties and obligations of the various arms of government and their agencies
relate each arm to its functions
appreciate how these arms interrelate

subtopics.name: Relationships among the arms of government

topics.name: Structures of Governance
objectives: compare the various political structures of governance

topics.name: Systems of Governance
objectives: distinguish between the different systems of governance

topics.name: Political Ideologies
objectives: differentiate between the major political ideologies
contrast their modes of production
topics.content: Communalism, Feudalism, Capitalism, Socialism, Communism, Totalitarianism, Fascism, Nazism.

topics.name: Constitution
objectives: define and identify sources and functions of constitutions
compare the nature of constitutions
topics.content: Meaning, sources, functions and types: written, unwritten, rigid and flexible.

topics.name: Principles of Democratic Government
objectives: identify the principles of democratic government
determine the application of these principles
topics.content: Ethics and accountability in public office, separation of power, checks and balances, individual and collective responsibility, constitutionalism, rule of law, representative government.

topics.name: Processes of Legislation
objectives: analyse the processes involved in the making of laws
topics.content: Legislative enactments: Acts, Edicts, Bye-laws, Delegated Legislation, Decrees.

topics.name: Citizenship
objectives: differentiate between the various methods of acquiring citizenship
specify the rights and responsibilities of a citizen
assess the obligations of the state

subtopics.name: Duties and obligations of the state

topics.name: The Electoral Process
objectives: distinguish the different types of franchise
identify and explain the types of electoral systems
analyse the various electoral processes

subtopics.name: Election: types and ingredients of a free and fair election
Electoral System: types, advantages and disadvantages of each

topics.name: Political Parties and Party Systems
objectives: assess the role of political parties
distinguish between types of party systems

topics.name: Pressure Groups
objectives: evaluate the functions and the modus operandi of pressure groups
distinguish between pressure groups and political parties

subtopics.name: Pressure groups: definition, types, functions and modes of operation
Differences between pressure groups and political parties

topics.name: Public Opinion
objectives: compare methods of assessing public opinion
assess the functions of public opinion
analyse the limitations of public opinion

subtopics.name: Public opinion: meaning, formation and measurement

topics.name: The Civil Service
objectives: analyse the significance of civil service in governance
topics.content: Definition, characteristics, functions, structure, control and problems.

topics.name: Pre-colonial Polities
objectives: appreciate the effectiveness of the pre-colonial political systems
compare pre-colonial systems of governance
topics.content: Pre-jihad Hausa, Emirate, Tiv, Igbo and Yoruba: their structural organization and the functions of their various political institutions.

topics.name: Imperialist Penetration
objectives: trace the processes of imperialist penetration
assess the impact of British and French policies
distinguish between British and French colonial practices

subtopics.name: Comparison of British and French colonial administration

topics.name: Process of Decolonization
objectives: evaluate the process of decolonization
assess the roles of nationalist leaders and parties
assess the impact of external forces and ideas (Pan-Africanism, Back-to-Africa Movements, Second World War etc)

topics.name: Constitutional Development in Nigeria
objectives: compare the various constitutional developments
topics.content: Features, merits and demerits of the Hugh Clifford Constitution (1922), Arthur Richards Constitution (1946), John Macpherson Constitution (1951), Oliver Lyttleton Constitution (1954) and the Independence Constitution (1960).

topics.name: Post-Independence Constitutions
objectives: assess the workings of the various constitutions
topics.content: The 1963, 1979, 1989 and 1999 constitutions: characteristics and shortcomings.

topics.name: Institutions of Government in Post-Independence Nigeria
objectives: evaluate the operations of the arms of government and their agencies, e.g. the civil service, armed forces, police, courts and others

subtopics.name: The Legislative (post-independence): structures, functions and workings
The Executive (post-independence): structure, functions and workings
The Judiciary (post-independence): structure, functions and workings

topics.name: Public Commissions Established by the 1979 and Subsequent Constitutions
objectives: evaluate the operations of public commissions
assess the problems of the Public Commissions and their constraints
topics.content: The Civil Service Commission, the Public Complaints Commission, Electoral Commissions, National Boundary Commission and others: objectives, functions and problems.

topics.name: Political Parties and Party Politics in Post-Independence Nigeria
objectives: contrast political processes in the republics
evaluate the ideologies, structure and composition of the political parties

topics.name: The Structure and Workings of Nigerian Federalism
objectives: examine the workings of Nigerian federalism
identify its problems
evaluate the corrective measures to be adopted

subtopics.name: Tiers of government and their relationship
Problems of Nigerian Federalism and solutions

topics.name: Public Corporations and Parastatals
objectives: examine the operations of public corporations and parastatals
identify the processes involved in privatization and commercialization
assess the economic importance of privatization and commercialization

subtopics.name: Public corporations: definition, types, purpose and functions
Finance, control and problems of public corporations
Comparison between public corporations and parastatals

topics.name: Local Government
objectives: trace the evolution and structure of local government
identify the major problems faced by local governments

subtopics.name: Problems of local government administration in Nigeria

topics.name: The Military in Nigerian Politics
objectives: evaluate the reasons given for military intervention
assess the achievements of military rule
determine the conditions that necessitated withdrawal from governance

subtopics.name: Factors that led to military intervention

topics.name: Foreign Policy
objectives: define foreign policy, identify and explain its determinants
topics.content: Definition, purpose, determining factors; formulation and implementation.

topics.name: Nigeria’s Foreign Policy
objectives: identify the major objectives of Nigeria’s foreign policy
analyse Nigeria’s non-aligned posture

topics.name: Nigeria’s Relations with African Countries
objectives: evaluate the role of Nigeria in continental affairs
assess the role of NEPAD in developing Africa

subtopics.name: Africa as the “centre piece” of Nigeria’s foreign policy

topics.name: Nigeria in International Organizations
objectives: analyse the dynamics of Nigeria’s involvement in international organizations
assess their contribution to the development of Nigeria

subtopics.name: The Organization of African Unity (Nigeria’s membership)
The Economic Community of West African States (Nigeria’s membership)
The Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries (Nigeria’s membership)

topics.name: International Organizations
objectives: evaluate the operations of these international organizations
assess the role of these organizations in world affairs
appreciate the challenges of these organizations and how they can be overcome
topics.content: For each organization: origin, objectives, structure, functions, achievements, problems and prospects.
